extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international affairs, diplomacy, and Cold War-era disarmament issues
extracted.subtask_short: news reporting on disarmament and diplomacy
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper article reporting on international disarmament commission proposals, diplomatic moves (including a Soviet draft German peace treaty), and related investigations (e.g., alleged germ warfare inquiries). Contains quoted recommendations, demands, and procedural expectations for commissions and investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans for progressive annual reduction of armed forces and armaments
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for the progressive annual reduction of all armed forces and all armaments, including verifying this census.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an item submitted to the commission; implies that disarmament programs should include concrete, year-by-year reduction plans and mechanisms to verify force/armament inventories (a census).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification methods (census) for armed forces and armaments
rubrics_metrics.description: Including verifying this census (i.e., mechanisms to confirm declared numbers of forces and armaments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the need for trustworthy methods to verify the counts of forces and weapons as part of any reduction plan; verification is a prerequisite for credible disarmament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of calculating and fixing limits on armed forces and armaments
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods of calculating and fixing limits on all armed forces and all armaments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires agreed technical/analytical procedures to determine allowable force and weapon levels and to set binding quantitative limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement on numerical limits for military establishments and implementation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The development of agreed numbers any military establishment might have and methods of carrying out those limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for consensus on concrete numeric ceilings for military establishments plus practical procedures for implementing and enforcing those ceilings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of an international control organ and proper safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: The establishment of an international control organ and proper safeguards before the timetable for giving effect to the disarmament program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disarmament should be overseen by an international body with appropriate safeguards in place; this institutional mechanism must be defined prior to implementing the timetable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear timetable for implementing the disarmament program
rubrics_metrics.description: A timetable for giving effect to the disarmament program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disarmament proposals should specify a schedule for phased implementation so progress and compliance can be measured against explicit dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for investigators of alleged germ warfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should form a committee offering 'every guarantee of moral and scientific independence' and be 'highly qualified in epidemiology.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigating allegations (e.g., germ warfare), appoint independent, scientifically credible investigators; highlight moral/scientific independence and domain expertise (epidemiology) to ensure legitimacy and acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soviet demand: end to the division of Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: The Soviet-U.S.S.R. draft demanded an end to the division of Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a core term in the Soviet draft peace treaty, reunification (ending division) is presented as a primary objective to be included in a negotiated settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soviet demand: withdrawal of occupation forces within a year after the treaty takes effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal of occupation forces from Germany within a year after the treaty takes effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft treaty sets a firm timeline for the removal of occupation troops, making rapid restoration of sovereignty a negotiating demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soviet demand: final establishment of Germany's frontiers per Potsdam Conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Final establishment of Germany's frontiers in accordance with the 1945 Potsdam Conference decisions; the proposed treaty must not take territory from Poland or give it to Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Territorial arrangements are to be fixed by reference to Potsdam; this clause asserts that postwar border decisions (e.g., Oder-Neisse) should be final and respected in any peace treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soviet demand: German pledge not to enter hostile coalitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A pledge by Germany that she will not enter any coalition aimed at any power which fought against the Germans in the last alliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft conditions include a political/military clause limiting Germany's international alignments to prevent future aggression toward former adversaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on German rearmament tied to treaty-established needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Germany may be permitted to make weapons, ammunition, etc., but this will be limited to the needs of such forces and 'must not go beyond' forces established by the peace treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any allowance for German forces/weapons must be strictly bounded by treaty-determined force levels; rearmament must be proportional and constrained by the peace settlement.
